speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand the severity and cause, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they started suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That recent self-resolving knee pain and your camping trip in Minnesota are concerning; could you describe the appearance of your wrist skin lesions and how they look compared to any other spots?

REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_lesions_wrist
REQUEST TEST: Syphilis_serology

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_lesions_wrist: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm. Syphilis_serology: Data not available (Requested tests not performed in provided data).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The suggestion of iron deficiency anemia does not fit with your high fever, acute wrist pain, and skin lesions; we must investigate the joint and systemic causes first. Can you tell me if these skin lesions are painful or itchy, and have you noticed any rash on your legs or palms?

REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff, ESR, CRP
REQUEST TEST: Lyme_disease_serology
REQUEST TEST: Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: CBC_with_diff: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; ESR: Not available; CRP: Not available; Lyme_disease_serology: Not available; Rheumatoid_Factor: Not available; Anti_CCP: Not available.

Note: Previous data indicates Joint_Asperation_Left_Wrist showed WBC >50,000 /μL and Gram-negative diplococci, and STI_Screen was positive for Gonorrhea. Skin lesions are described as painless.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Arthritis (Neisseria gonorrhoeae).

The clinical picture of a sexually active 17-year-old with migratory joint pain, wrist arthritis, fever, and skin lesions is classic for this infection, confirmed by your positive gonorrhea screen and the presence of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint aspirate. The "painless" nature of the lesions is consistent with the sterile, vasculitic petechiae often seen in this condition.

REQUEST TEST: Gonococcal_Culture_from_Joint_Aspirate_and_Blood_Culture
